title: add spectral-sensitivity canary to detect phase-shifted throughput/latency anomalies
author: Priya Karthik
description:
Motivation: We observe a class of false positives and missed regressions when traffic has strong periodic components (cron-driven spikes, nightly batch windows) or when request routing causes phase-shifted latency/throughput patterns across regions. Existing canary detectors that operate purely on time-domain deltas or percentile shifts either overreact to periodic noise or ignore slowly drifting phase-shifts that presage capacity saturation. This PR introduces a spectral-sensitivity canary heuristic that augments the existing ensemble by analysing short FFT fingerprints of latency/throughput windows to surface phase-shifted anomalies and reduce periodic-noise false positives.

Design summary:
- Compute sliding-window FFT on aligned per-route throughput and p95 latency time series (window=5m, step=30s by default).
- Extract dominant frequency bands and phase offsets; compress to a lightweight fingerprint (top-3 frequency bins + relative phase vector).
- Compare candidate canary window fingerprint to baseline (rolling 24h fingerprint atlas) using cosine similarity + phase-delta penalty.
- Combine spectral similarity score with existing time-domain anomaly score via weighted fusion (configurable weights, default 0.6 time-domain / 0.4 spectral).
- Auto-tune spectral threshold by sampling recent baselines for periodicity strength; if baseline shows strong periodicity, spectral weight increases to avoid false positives, otherwise time-domain weight remains dominant.

Implementation notes:
- New module perf_canary/spectral_sensitivity.py implements FFT fingerprinting with numpy FFT (fallback to rfft on constrained environments).
- Added canary config flags: spectral_enabled (bool), spectral_window_secs, spectral_step_secs, spectral_weight, spectral_threshold, spectral_atlas_retention.
- Atlas stored as compressed protobuf lines in /canary/atlas per-route; retention defaults to 48h.
- Integration point: added as a post-score fusion step in canary_evaluator.evaluate_window().

Testing and evaluation:
- Unit tests: tests/perf_canary/test_spectral_sensitivity.py covering fingerprint stability, similarity scoring, and weight fusion edge cases.
- Integration: perf-canary smoke job added to CI that runs synthetic periodic workloads (cron-like 5m spikes) and phase-shifted traffic to verify reduced churn.

Results:
- On a corpus of production-sampled routes with known nightly spikes (N=120 routes), false-positive rate dropped from 18.7% to 12.3% (~34% relative reduction) when spectral_enabled=true.
- Detection latency for phase-shift regressions improved median 12% (0.9m faster detection) while preserving true positive rate within ±2%.

Backwards compatibility and rollout:
- Feature is off by default for existing tenants.
- Configurable rollout: can enable per-team, per-org, or globally via console flag.
- Added safety guard: if fusion score triggers canary but spectral fingerprint is unstable (atlas coverage < 3 baseline windows), the detector falls back to time-domain only and marks the result as provisional.

Operational concerns and follow-ups:
- Atlas retention and fingerprint storage increase metadata size; we estimate ~0.5MB per active route per day; added sampling and TTL options.
- We will monitor new metrics: canary.spectral.matches, canary.spectral.false_positive_rate, canary.spectral.atlas_coverage.
- Follow-up PR planned to offload heavy FFT to Rust accelerated crate and to add GPU-accelerated batched FFT for high-cardinality routes.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation code
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration smoke in CI
- [x] Docs: canary spectral section in docs/perf-canary.md
- [x] Rollout config and console toggle

Related: ENG-91234, SUP-2418. Refer to internal doc: /docs/observability/spectral-canary-notes.md for extended evaluation graphs.

review_comments: Marco Liu: Can we avoid per-request FFT by bucketing at 10s resolution? Also please add complexity analysis (O(n log n) per window) — answered: we use 30s step and window=5m to amortize cost; added complexity note and optional sampling path.

Aisha Banerjee: How do we avoid atlas poisoning when an on-call mitigation run creates long-tail changes? Suggest a rollback decay — answered: implemented atlas retention and provisional marker when atlas coverage is low; added decay TTL and manual purge endpoints.
Diego Ramos: CI flakes on CI job 3/8 — looks like test used float randomness; please seed RNG — answered: fixed by seeding and added deterministic fixtures; reran CI.
Security review (infra): Ensure atlas blobs have access controls — addressed: atlas stored in internal metadata bucket with org-level ACLs; noted in infra change.
QA: Please sketch expected visualization panels for console — added docs section with sample panels and alert thresholds.
Priya (author): Responded to all comments, added follow-up task ENG-92011 to add Rust FFT acceleration.
merge_summary: Merged via squash on 2025-02-20 after CI green and approvals from Marco and Aisha. Changeset squashed into a single commit a9f7b2 and backend migrations applied. No runtime breaking changes; feature gated behind spectral_enabled flag.
release_notes: Add a new spectral-sensitivity canary heuristic to reduce periodic-noise false positives and detect phase-shifted performance regressions. Disabled by default; opt-in via canary config or console feature flag. Monitor canary.spectral.* metrics after enabling.
